# Liquid Cooling Guide

> Independent technical reference on liquid cooling for micro data centers: how it works, the formulas, and a sourced comparison of small-scale cooling cabinets. One concept per page, worked examples with real numbers, live calculators. Data compiled from manufacturer pages, datasheets and trade press only; unpublished prices are marked, never invented.
> Published by Friovia, a liquid-cooling cabinet maker. Editorial policy: every claim sourced; vendors listed whether we compete or not; no paid placements.

Locales:

- [English /](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/): default locale, full site (en covers all content; es/ar are localized landings).
  - [Español](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/es): es landing page (localized hero, toolbar and directory navigation).
  - [العربية](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/ar): ar landing page (localized hero, toolbar and directory navigation, RTL).

Radar:

- [Industry radar](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/news): dated items across technology, products, investment and standards — every entry links to its source — plus the curated milestone timeline (STULZ×CoolIT 2017, ASHRAE W-classes 2019, 3M PFAS exit 2022-2025, GB200-era racks and ORv3 2024, SS 726:2026).
- [State of liquid cooling 2026](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/state-of-liquid-cooling-2026): the annual digest — direct-to-chip default above 30 kW, PG25 wins the fluid question, standards consolidated, tropics become the main event, and the 20-50 kW turnkey gap persists.

Basics:

  - [Rack configurator](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/playground/configurator): scenario → node platform → CDU & pump operating point → thermal chain → calculation note — two node platforms (OAI 8-OAM tray; HGX H100/H200-class 8-GPU node); the open-source kernel picks the best-evidenced CDU from its sourced curve library, holds the flow window with an automatic pump setpoint, traces the system curve, reports any run outside its evidenced data domain as not judgeable (bit-identical parity gate in CI), and screens the rack builder's catalog by nameplate; dew-point red line, ASHRAE W-class, downloadable calc note.
- [Playground](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/playground): Interactive tools — rack configurator, rack builder, capacity derating simulator, room load calculator. All computation in-browser; formulas shown with user values substituted.
  - [Rack builder](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/playground/rack-builder): assemble a rack from server types, set room temperature, get liquid/air heat split, derated cabinet capacity, coolant flow (L/min), room AC requirement and verdicts.
  - [Derating simulator](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/playground/derating): capacity-vs-ambient curve, approach-temperature model anchored to Vertiv XDU070 published data (86.5 kW @ 45°C coolant / 25°C air).
  - [Room load calculator](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/playground/room-load): 1.1× IT-load rule, refrigeration-ton conversion, spare-capacity margin verdict.
- [What is liquid cooling?](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/what-is-liquid-cooling): Direct-to-chip liquid cooling explained — cold plates, CDUs, manifolds, UQD quick disconnects, PG25 fluid, and the standards that matter (OCP, ASHRAE, IEC 62368-1, SS 726).
- [What is a CDU?](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/what-is-a-cdu): The coolant distribution unit — pumps, heat exchangers, TCS vs facility water loops, in-rack/in-row/facility form factors, liquid-to-air vs liquid-to-liquid trade-offs.
- [L2A vs L2L](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/liquid-to-air-vs-liquid-to-liquid): the CDU form-factor axis — liquid-to-air rejects heat into room air (sealed, no facility water, the 20-50 kW micro-DC band); liquid-to-liquid hands it to facility water and scales to megawatts. Room rule 1.1 × IT vs W-classes.
- [What is a micro data center?](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/what-is-a-micro-data-center): the self-contained enclosure definition, the size spectrum from server closet (Uptime: ~10% of enterprise IT) to 150 kW lights-out pods, and the 20-50 kW density gap.
- [Cold plate vs immersion cooling](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/cold-plate-vs-immersion): The two architectures compared — heat capture (60-80% vs ~100%), fluids and PFAS regulation, serviceability, standards, floor loading.
- [Glossary](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/glossary): 50+ self-contained, anchorable definitions: DLC, CDU, TCS, FWS, UQD, blind-mate, ORv3, L2A/L2L, W-class, approach temperature, capture ratio, derating, wet-bulb, PUE, PG25, TDP, N+1, floor loading, COP.

Formulas (one formula per page: definition → formula → worked example with real numbers → live calculator → common mistakes):

- [Engineering & calculators channel](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/engineering): hub for every formula with a live tool — load budgets, flow, derating, W-classes, room AC, UQD, fluids, pressure drop.
- [Coolant flow rate](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/coolant-flow-rate): flow [L/min] = P [kW] × 60 / (4.186 × ΔT [°C]) — 50 kW at ΔT 8 °C needs 89.6 L/min. Use liquid-captured heat (60-80% of IT load), not total.
- [Heat capture split](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/heat-capture-split): P_liquid = capture × P_IT — direct-to-chip captures 60-80%; the 20-40% air share still needs room AC sized on the total.
- [TDP → rack kW](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/tdp-to-rack-kw): P_rack ≈ nodes × (Σ GPU + Σ CPU TDP) × 1.2 — 8×1 kW GPUs + 2×360 W CPUs = 10.5 kW/node; 42 kW/rack example.
- [Room AC load](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/room-ac-load): the 1.1× rule — an L2A cabinet needs room air conditioning sized at 1.1 × IT load; 30 kW rack → 33 kW ≈ 9.4 refrigeration tons.
- [kW ↔ refrigeration tons](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/kw-to-tons): 1 ton = 3.517 kW = 12,000 BTU/h; tons = kW ÷ 3.517. Cooling tons ≠ electrical draw (COP ≈ 3).
- [Approach temperature & derating](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/approach-temperature): approach = coolant supply °C − room air °C; capacity scales roughly linearly with it — 86.5 kW @ 45 °C/25 °C (Vertiv XDU070) halves at 35 °C air, collapses below ~5 °C approach.
- [Pressure drop](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/pressure-drop): Darcy–Weisbach ΔP = f × (L/D) × ρv²/2 — 90 L/min through 25 mm hose loses ≈20 kPa over 3 m; velocity enters squared.
- [Floor loading](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/floor-loading): load = mass × 9.81 ÷ footprint — 1,200 kg on 600 × 1,200 mm prints 16.4 kN/m², ~5× office design loads.
- [PUE math](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/pue-math): PUE = total ÷ IT energy; 100 kW IT + 15 kW overhead = 1.15. What it hides: climate (wet-bulb), the IT term itself, and the cabinet-in-a-room boundary.
- [ASHRAE W-classes](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/ashrae-w-classes): W17/W27/W32/W40/W45 — the number ≈ max facility water supply °C; higher classes buy free-cooling hours; lookup included.
- [Wet-bulb & free cooling](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/wet-bulb-free-cooling): free cooling needs wet-bulb + ~6 K ≤ required coolant temperature; tropical 28-30 °C wet-bulbs leave no margin even at W45.

Choosing:

- [Liquid cooling vs air](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/liquid-cooling-vs-air): When liquid becomes necessary (and the 30 kW crossover myth), tropical derating physics, room AC load math, what PUE comparisons assume.
- [Cooling cabinet comparison](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/cabinet-comparison): Verified comparison of rack-level products from Schneider, Vertiv, STULZ×CoolIT, Rittal, Asetek, nVent — power class, cooling type, facility requirements, per-row sources. Documents the 20-50 kW turnkey gap.
- [What drives the cost](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/liquid-cooling-cost): Why prices aren't published; the cost stack (capacity, architecture, redundancy, monitoring, certification, install); how to compare quotes fairly.
- [RFQ scope checklist](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/rfq-scope-checklist): 12 line items that make quotes comparable — capacity at your ambient, capture ratio, redundancy, interconnects, monitoring, acceptance testing, written derating curves.
- [Liquid-ready servers](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/liquid-ready-servers): The five compatibility checks — cold plate coverage, UQD couplings, ASHRAE W-class, flow/pressure, serviceability — and why open interfaces prevent lock-in.
- [Hot & tropical climates](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/liquid-cooling-hot-climates): Derating physics with published numbers (Vertiv XDU070: ~half capacity from 25°C to 35°C ambient), free-cooling failure at high wet-bulb, SS 726:2026 scope, hot-climate buying checklist.

Deploy & Ops:

- [Site survey](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/site-survey): the six-point checklist — floor loading, electrical, heat egress (1.1×), water, access, noise — each linked to its formula.
- [Room load calculation](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/room-load-calculation): Whether a room can host an L2A cabinet — the 1.1× IT-load rule, kW-to-ton conversion (÷3.52), a worked hospital example, and the full site survey.
- [Commissioning](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/commissioning): 8-step acceptance sequence — dry pressure test, fill/purge, flow and ΔT verification, pressure survey, dew-point check, leak-system test, load ramp, baseline snapshot.
- [Leaks: risk, detection, response](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/liquid-cooling-leaks): Where leaks actually happen (couplings, clamps, corrosion), how dripless UQD and blind-mate designs mitigate them, the four-layer detection/response model.
- [Maintenance schedule](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/maintenance-schedule): Intervals table — weekly visual, monthly trending, quarterly filters, semi-annual fluid analysis, annual coupling/sensor work, vendor fluid replacement.

  - [Fortum profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/fortum): vendor profile — Fortum recovers waste heat from Microsoft's Espoo and Kirkkonummi data centres into its district heating network; in May 2026 it started heat pump production expected to cover about 40% of the area's heat.
  - [Dalkia profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/dalkia): vendor profile — Dalkia, an EDF Group energy services company, runs French district heating networks and data-centre energy services, recovering waste heat from data centres such as the Meteo France supercomputer site in Toulouse.
  - [Helen profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/helen): vendor profile — Helen, owned by the City of Helsinki, has recovered data-centre waste heat into its district heating network since 2010; in August 2026 it signed to add a new data centre supplying over 500,000 MWh of heat per year.
  - [Eurovent profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/eurovent): vendor profile — European HVACR industry association; published the Guidebook on Data Centre Cooling (November 2026), and Eurovent Certita Certification operates the ITCU programme certifying CRAC, CRAH and rear-door IT cooling units.
  - [DLB Associates profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/dlb-associates): vendor profile — US data-centre engineering firm (founded 1980); publishes a liquid-cooling series on cold plates and CDUs; Accenture closed its 65% majority-stake acquisition in January 2026.
  - [Future-tech profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/future-tech): vendor profile — UK data-centre engineering consultancy listing direct chip cooling among its cooling solutions; M&E designs for direct liquid cooling since 2012; joined Nscale in December 2025.
  - [Exascale Labs profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/exascale-labs): vendor profile — Nasdaq-listed (XLAB) AI infrastructure provider in San Francisco; its factory-built Modular Data Centers pre-integrate power, cooling and networking; non-binding LOI with Compal for a US 800 VDC validation platform.
  - [EkkoSense profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/ekkosense): vendor profile — UK software company (founded 2013, PE-backed) whose EkkoSoft Critical platform monitors temperatures and flow rates across direct-to-chip, rear-door heat exchanger and hybrid liquid-cooled infrastructure.
  - [Ramboll profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/ramboll): vendor profile — Engineering consultancy advising data-centre owners on adopting liquid cooling and heat reuse; 15+ GW of data-centre capacity designed and tested and 1,000+ studies completed.
  - [RED Engineering Design profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/red-engineering-design): vendor profile — Engineering consultancy within Tractebel (ENGIE Group) designing liquid-cooled AI factories and HPC facilities, including a 40MW hybrid data centre in Johor Bahru, Malaysia.
  - [Salute profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/salute): vendor profile — Data-center services company operating AI/HPC liquid cooling: full-service direct-to-chip operations launched at NVIDIA GTC Washington DC in 2025, expected to support roughly 250 MW, then about 3,100 MW more by end-2027.
  - [HITT Contracting profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/hitt-contracting): vendor profile — Virginia general contractor founded 1937; builds and retrofits liquid-cooled data centers, citing cold-plate loops that support up to 160 kW per rack versus 10 kW per rack with air cooling.
  - [NESIC profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/nesic): vendor profile — NEC-group network integrator in Japan demonstrating data-center liquid cooling: two-phase direct-to-chip in an air-cooled data center (2024) and immersion testing with 94% lower cooling energy (2023).
  - [Legrand profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/legrand): vendor profile — Data-centre cooling via Legrand brands: Minkels row-based coolers and USystems ColdLogik rear-door heat exchangers (CL20/CL21/CL23) recommended for high-density HPC applications.
  - [Stantec profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/stantec): vendor profile — Engineering and design firm whose UK team publishes liquid-cooling guidance for AI-era data centre heat loads and cites hybrid direct-to-chip work such as the NTT Garland, Texas campus.
  - [Sweco profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/sweco): vendor profile — European engineering firm (about 23,000 experts) whose Finnish team delivered the Borealis Kajaani campus in 2025: site-wide megawatt-scale direct liquid cooling with waste heat into district heating.
  - [ToffeeX profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/toffeex): vendor profile — London-based physics-driven generative design software (Imperial College London spinout) that creates GPU/CPU cold plates, manifold and heat exchanger geometries for AI data centre cooling.
  - [Sunbird Software profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/sunbird-software): vendor profile — DCIM software vendor whose dcTrack platform provides CDU modeling and telemetry, manifold modeling and liquid port tracking; dcTrack 9.3.5 shipped 6 July 2026 with liquid cooling features.
  - [Southland Industries profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/southland-industries): vendor profile — US MEP design-build firm (founded 1949) with 40+ GW of data center capacity constructed; delivered proprietary liquid-cooled racks for two 6 MW Oregon data vaults and a 24 MW waterless-cooled Texas facility.
  - [World Wide Technology profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/world-wide-technology): vendor profile — St. Louis technology integrator (14,000+ employees) that tests direct-to-chip and two-phase liquid cooling in its Advanced Technology Center labs and advises on data center water efficiency.
  - [Valicor profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/valicor): vendor profile — Environmental services firm (Monroe, Ohio; founded 1982) handling liquid-cooled data center commissioning flushwater, glycol, hydrotest and chemical cleaning wastewater via 250+ trucks in 16 states.
  - [Stockholm Exergi profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/stockholm-exergi): vendor profile — Stockholm district heating utility (owned by the City of Stockholm and Ankhiale) that buys data center excess heat via Open District Heating and Stockholm Data Parks, currently heating 11,000 apartments.
  - [Sudlows profile](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/supply-chain/sudlows): vendor profile — UK data centre design and build firm (Manchester, founded 2014) that engineered NTT's production immersion and direct-contact liquid cooling deployment in India; Kent plc bought Sudlows Consulting in 2025.
- [UQD quick disconnects](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/uqd-quick-disconnects): The OCP UQD family UQD04–UQD40 (number ≈ nominal L/min); size table, dripless and blind-mate mechanics, the pressure-drop trap.
- [ORv3 manifold spec](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/orv3-manifold): the OCP Open Rack V3 blind-mate manifold quoted — 50 psig working pressure, 60 °C max fluid, PG25, ≤5% flow distribution target, 24-valve reference design, W45-class 17–65 °C operation, plus the OAI 1.25–2.0 L/min/kW flow rules and what the spec deliberately does not publish.
- [Fluids & PFAS](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/liquid-cooling-fluids): PG25 vs oils vs fluorinated fluids — PFAS regulation, 3M's 2025 exit, transport/disposal rules, loop maintenance.
- [Standards](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/liquid-cooling-standards): OCP interconnects (UQD, ORv3 manifold Rev 1.0), ASHRAE W-classes (W17-W45), IEC 62368-1 Ed.4 liquid clauses, SS 726:2026 — mapped to a buying checklist.
- [SS 726 deep dive](https://liquidcoolingguide.com/ss726-liquid-cooling-standard): The world's first tropical liquid cooling standard (Singapore, Aug 2026), explained from the official preview and launch release — verbatim scope (direct-to-chip; rear-door/indirect and two-phase excluded), clause structure, OCP/ASHRAE references, working group (STT GDC, AirTrunk, Meta, OCP), immersion annex, scope limits for edge deployments.
